result.name: MS17-010 EternalBlue SMB Remote Code Execution
result.description: The remote host is missing the MS17-010 security update which fixes critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in the Windows SMBv1 server. The EternalBlue exploit targeting this vulnerability was used in the WannaCry and NotPetya ransomware campaigns.
result.solution: Apply Microsoft Security Bulletin MS17-010 immediately. Disable SMBv1 if the patch cannot be applied immediately. Block inbound TCP port 445 at the network perimeter.

result.name: Windows Print Spooler RCE (PrintNightmare)
result.description: The Windows Print Spooler service is vulnerable to remote code execution. An authenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability to run arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges on a vulnerable system.
result.solution: Apply the latest cumulative update from Microsoft. Consider disabling the Print Spooler service on Domain Controllers and systems that do not require printing.

result.name: Telnet Cleartext Authentication
result.description: The Telnet service is running and accepting connections. Telnet transmits all data including authentication credentials in cleartext, allowing network eavesdroppers to capture passwords and session data.
result.solution: Disable the Telnet service and migrate all remote access to SSH. Ensure SSH is configured with key-based authentication and has root login disabled.

result.name: SSL/TLS: Deprecated TLS 1.0 Protocol Enabled
result.description: The remote server is configured to accept connections using the deprecated TLS 1.0 protocol. TLS 1.0 is vulnerable to the BEAST attack and has other known cryptographic weaknesses. PCI DSS 3.2 and above requires TLS 1.0 to be disabled.
result.solution: Disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 on the server. Enable only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. Update cipher suites to exclude CBC-mode ciphers where possible.

result.name: Missing HTTP Security Headers
result.description: The web server response is missing several recommended security headers: - Content-Security-Policy (CSP) not set - X-Frame-Options not set (clickjacking risk) - X-Content-Type-Options not set - Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) not set These missing headers increase the attack surface for client-side attacks.
result.solution: Configure the web server to send appropriate security headers. Add Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Strict-Transport-Security headers to all HTTP responses.

result.name: Default Credentials: admin/admin (Web Interface)
result.description: The administrative web interface is accessible using default credentials (admin/admin or admin/password). Default credentials allow any unauthenticated attacker to gain full administrative access to the device or application.
result.solution: Immediately change all default credentials to strong, unique passwords. Implement account lockout after failed login attempts. Consider restricting administrative access to trusted IP ranges only.

result.name: Apache Log4j2 JNDI Remote Code Execution (Log4Shell)
result.description: The remote host is running a version of Apache Log4j2 that is vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell). An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted request containing a JNDI lookup string to achieve remote code execution.
result.solution: Update Log4j2 to version 2.17.1 or later (Java 8), 2.12.4 (Java 7), or 2.3.2 (Java 6). As an immediate mitigation, set -Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true in the JVM arguments. Identify all applications using Log4j2 as a dependency.

result.name: Redis Server Accessible Without Authentication
result.description: A Redis server is accessible without authentication. Unauthenticated access to Redis allows an attacker to read and write all cached data, execute arbitrary Lua scripts, and potentially escalate to remote code execution by writing malicious cron jobs or SSH keys.
result.solution: Enable Redis authentication (requirepass) in redis.conf. Bind Redis to localhost or an internal network interface only. Use a firewall to block external access to port 6379. Consider running Redis in a protected-mode configuration.
